{{Quote|Every man, woman, and child on Nathema died that day. Every beast, bird, and fish; all the insects and plants; every living being touched by the Force was consumed. When the ritual ended, Nathema was no longer a world. It was a husk sucked dry. Lord Vitiate sacrificed millions, stealing their life force to make himself immortal.|Darth Nyriss|<ref name="Revan" />}}
The '''Ritual of Nathema''' was the name given by [[Historian/Legends|historians]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] to the event in [[4999 BBY]], in which the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] performed a [[Sith Emperor's ritual|dark ritual]] that stripped [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] itself from the entire [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Nathema]]. While Imperial historians saw it as one of the greatest achievements in the history of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Old Sith Empire]], the Ritual was actually the result of Vitiate's [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|mental enslavement]] of over eight thousand [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lords]]. Vitiate, with his colossal power bent them to his will and absorbed their power as part of the ritual that devastated the planet and rendered himself [[Immortality/Legends|immortal]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|But in the aftermath of the war&mdash;after our defeat at the hands of the Republic and our flight to escape the massacre of our people by the Jedi&mdash;he emerged from his solitude to call a great council of all the Sith Lords who remained.|Darth Nyriss|<ref name="Revan" />}}
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] was destroyed by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in the [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion]], and the people of the Empire were terrified that the Republic and their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] protectors would not stop until the entire [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was wiped out.<ref name="Revan" /> [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]] was in the process of orchestrating a purge of the remnants of the Empire,<ref name="History 30">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 30: Rise of the Sith Emperor}}</ref><ref name="SWTORE110">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="TEA128">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref><ref name="TEGtW37">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> and the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] chose to take advantage of the people's fear. Broadcasting speeches across the Empire that described how the Jedi would not rest until the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] were destroyed, Vitiate stoked the Empire's terror and then offered them hope:<ref name="Revan" /> arriving on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]],<ref name="Codex" /> Vitiate sent out a call for all of the remaining Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lords]] to meet with him on his world [[Nathema]], where he promised to lead them in a powerful ritual of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] that would ensure the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order's]] destruction. However, Vitiate ordered his [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] and researchers to locate a world upon which the Empire could rebuild without fear of the Jedi following.<ref name="Revan" />

==The Ritual==
{{Quote|He turned them into slaves to his will, forcing them to participate in the most complex ritual of Sith sorcery ever attempted. Calling on the dark side, Lord Vitiate devoured them. He fed on their power, absorbing it into himself, utterly obliterating all traces of his victims.|Darth Nyriss|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Zildrog_on_Nathema.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Zildrog, an ancient superweapon from Iokath, was used in the ritual.]]
In [[4999 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> not long after he returned to Nathema,<ref name="Codex" /> Vitiate was informed by the [[Unidentified Sith researcher|head researcher]] that they had discovered a [[Kamat Krote|hyperlane]] connecting Korriban and the long-lost colony world of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]. Three [[Standard day/Legends|days]] later, Vitiate announced the commencement of his ritual,<ref name="Revan" /> and eight thousand Sith Lords answered his call,<ref name="Codex" /> including the surviving members of the Empire's ruling [[Sith Council]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> However, as each Sith arrived at [[Vitiate's palace|his palace]], Vitiate [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|dominated their minds]] and bound their wills to his own with his immense power, placing their strength at his disposal. He then began the [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]] itself, which took ten days to perform.<ref name="Revan" /> To achieve his goal, Vitiate used the central computer of [[Zildrog]], an ancient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] from the artificial world of [[Iokath]] that specialized in the transfer of life energies, to assist in the ritual.<ref name="Zildrog" /> The ritual conferred [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]] upon Vitiate, granting him immense strength in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] at the expense of the entire world.<ref name="Revan" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|He lured many Sith Lords here before consuming them in a dark ritual that wiped out all life on the planet.|Lord Dramath|<ref name="KOTET 7">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=7}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ritual_of_Nathema.png|thumb|left|260px|The surface of Nathema after the devastation]]
The only species on Nathema that survived the cataclysm were the [[voreclaw]], [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] insectoid bipeds who lived underground. The voreclaw [[Hive mind/Legends|hive mind]] was obliterated by the ritual, leaving their colonies nothing more than groups of mindless individuals, who eventually emerged onto the surface driven by the hunger. In the utter absence of any other food, the creatures turned to [[cannibalism]], attacking and eating each other until Vitiate captured the few remaining survivors and stored them in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] beneath the [[Sanitarium]].<ref name="Voreclaw">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Voreclaw}}</ref> As a result of the Ritual, Nathema was left entirely devoid of the Force, and the physical environment of the planet itself was warped. [[Color/Legends|Color]] seemed to have leeched from reality to those who stood on its surface, and the planet's [[Nathema's sun|orange sun]] appeared to be a dull brown when viewed through the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The newly immortal Vitiate shed his mortal identity and took on the title of Sith Emperor, blaming the devastation of Nathema on the Jedi. He then proceeded to gather the younger generation of the Empire's people before embarking on a [[Sith exodus|twenty-year odyssey]] from Korriban to Dromund Kaas. After [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituting the Empire]] on Dromund Kaas, the Emperor purged all navigation data relating to Nathema in order to ensure that no one discovered the truth of Nathema's fate.<ref name="Revan" />

However, members of the Empire's ruling [[Dark Council]] eventually discovered the planet's existence and history over a thousand years after the Ritual, and they began a [[Nathema conspiracy|conspiracy]] to unseat the Emperor and ensure he would never commit such an atrocity again. The conspiracy was destroyed,<ref name="Revan" /> however, and by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Great Galactic War]] with the Republic three [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] later, the Ritual of Nathema was celebrated by Imperial [[Historian/Legends|historians]] as a great achievement. The historians were unaware of the actual events of the Ritual, believing that the other Sith Lords had willingly sacrificed their strength on the Emperor's behalf.<ref name="Codex" /> The Sith Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]], who had visited Nathema and learned the truth of the Emperor's rise from the conspirator [[Darth Nyriss]],<ref name="Revan" /> dedicated himself to preventing the Emperor from performing the Sith ritual on a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] scale during the [[Galactic War]] between the Republic and the Empire, and he informed the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] of the Ritual's history in order to convince them of his sincerity.<ref name="Alliance">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|An Unthinkable Alliance|Tython}}</ref>

[[File:Nathema_from_Nathema_Conspiracy.jpg|thumb|280px|Life returns to Nathema]]
Vitiate meanwhile continued to use Nathema for his own purposes, as unknown to the Sith and the Dark Council he also secretly built another empire, the [[Eternal Empire]] on the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] planet of [[Zakuul]] under the name [[Valkorion]].<ref name="KOTET 7" /> Vitiate maintained a Sanitarium on Nathema, in which powerful Force-users who opposed him could be experimented upon, unable to draw on the Force to escape or resist.<ref name="Sanitarium">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|The Sanitarium}}</ref> The Sanitarium was guarded by [[Nathema Zealot]]s, a secretive group of powerful Force-sensitives able to withstand the horrors of the [[Force void/Legends|void in the Force]] through a regime of daily and intense rituals and meditation.<ref name="Nathema Zealots">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=codex|Nathema Zealots}}</ref> Vitiate kept the [[Dramath's holocron|holocron]] with the essence of his father [[Dramath]] in the [[Emperor's Vaults|vault]] beneath the Sanitarium,<ref name="KOTET 7" /> while another vault under an ancient Sith temple housed Zildrog, whom Vitiate had deactivated after the ritual.<ref name="Nathema">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|The Nathema Conspiracy}}</ref> Vitiate lived for over thirteen hundred years by [[Essence transfer|moving his consciousness]] between the [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|host bodies]],<ref name="Valkorion">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Valkorion}}</ref> but around [[3630 BBY]]<ref name="Date">{{TOR_updates|5}}</ref> his spirit was finally destroyed by the combined efforts of [[Alliance Commander|the Commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]] and Valkorion's biological children, [[Arcann]] and [[Vaylin]].<ref name="KOTET 9">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=9}}</ref> His death had a profound effect on Nathema, as the previously lifeless world was miraculously revitalized within a short time. Force-users no longer felt the unsettling "wrongness" upon setting foot on the planet, the air had become fresher, and the weather more dynamic. Most importantly, vibrant plant life from seeds left in the soil had not only taken root but flourished, dramatically altering the planet's once-desolate landscape.<ref name="Reborn">{{TORcite|type=codex|Nathema Reborn}}</ref> Escaped experiments from the Sanitarium gave Nathema some semblance of animal life,<ref name="Nathema" /> while surviving Zealots began settling in the abandoned wilds.<ref name="Zealots">{{TORcite|type=codex|Zealots Without a Master}}</ref> Though Nathema had returned to life, experts were unable to determine any precise environmental mechanism that could have brought about such an abrupt change.<ref name="Reborn" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Ritual of Nathema was first described in [[Drew Karpyshyn]]'s [[2011]] novel ''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]'', though it was not given a proper name until the release of the [[BioWare]]&ndash;[[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' later that year. One of the in-game [[Datacron/Legends|Datacrons]], [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]]-like devices that grant players permanent stat boosts, can be located in the [[Gorinth Canyon]] region on the Empire's version of [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]], and the corresponding Galactic History entry for the in-game Codex describes the Empire's account of the Ritual of Nathema.<ref name="Codex" /> The Ritual is also mentioned in the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] class mission "An Unthinkable Alliance" during the game, though Lord Scourge does not identify the planet's name.<ref name="Alliance" />

[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']], a reference book released alongside the game, features [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Gnost-Dural]]'s investigations into the history of the Emperor, though he was unable to determine exactly what occurred on Nathema.<ref name="Journal">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']]</ref> The [[2012]] reference guide ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' mentioned the event during its summary of Karpyshyn's novel,<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> and the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' also featured a mention of the Ritual.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Nathema was later featured in the game's [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']] expansion, in which the story of the Ritual was relayed once more by [[Force spirit]] of Vitiate's father Dramath.<ref name="KOTET 7" /> An update set after Vitiate's final death revisited the planet in "The Nathema Conspiracy" flashpoint, which added to the backstory of the Ritual by revealing Zildrog's involvement and showed the void in the Force dissipating and the planet returning to life, indicating that the effects of the Ritual were not irreversible, but rather lasted only for as long as Vitiate lived.<ref name="Nathema" />
